transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Tom Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Lucent VP Product), Ravi Shah (Lucent Head of ML), Nina Gomez (Lucent Platform Eng), Oliver Park (Lucent CFO)

Summary: Quick QBR / health check focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents last quarter, and product roadmap alignment (dedicated vs hosted, VPC options, KMS). Agreed next steps around sharing security docs, running a dedicated-capacity demo, and doing a targeted benchmark for the pilot workload.

Topics: usage & cost, latencies, error/retry patterns, model versions in production, caching/kv cache behavior, dedicated capacity discussion, security/compliance (SOC 2, KMS, SSO), roadmap & pilot next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alice: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about an hour, quick agenda — usage, cost, reliability, then roadmap and next steps. sound good?
[00:12] Maya: yep that's great, thanks.
[00:18] Ravi: thanks Alice, uh appreciate you doing this.
[00:25] Tom: hi all, Tom from Redwood, I'll jump into the performance bits and the dedicated capacity options later.
[00:33] Nina: quick note, we have the engineering folks on chat but not joined here, we'll pull them in if needed.

[02:05] Alice: ok first page — usage. last quarter we saw a 35% increase in monthly tokens for Lucent's captioning pipeline, most growth on peak hours. your average P95 latency on hosted endpoints is around 420ms for short-form prompts, is that roughly what you're seeing?
[02:18] Ravi: yeah that's in the ballpark, sometimes spikes to 700ms during campaign spikes. cost has been creeping up, our finance team flagged the embedding and rerank jobs as big drivers.
[03:02] Oliver: cost visibility is top for us — can you show the token breakouts again, and where caching helped?
[03:20] Priya: sure Oliver, we'll attach the per-route token breakdown after the call, Alice will send. we did enable prefix caching on a subset, that saved about 22% for repeated prompts.

[05:15] Tom: on reliability, we saw three incidents last quarter related to a region-level capacity throttling event — automatic fallback routed some traffic to a smaller variant which increased latencies. we patched routing policy thresholds, but recommended a canary for future rollouts.
[05:40] Maya: can you explain the fallback? did we lose requests or just slower responses?
[05:49] Tom: mostly slower responses, a small percentage had transient retries. no data leakage. fallback was to a quantized variant with slightly higher perplexity but lower resource needs. apologies if the product name was mangled in logs, the transcription shows KV cash sometimes.

[08:10] Ravi: about the quantized variant — we saw occasional quality regressions for longer context calls. is that expected?
[08:22] Tom: yes, quantization and some kernel paths can increase hallucination risk on long-form. our recommendation is to use dedicated capacity for consistent latency and pin a model version for the pilot, or apply hybrid routing: low-latency critical calls to full-precision, batchable jobs to quantized variant.

[11:00] Nina: on dedicated vs hosted — what's the lift and timeline? we need VPC peering, SSO, and KMS for key management.
[11:12] Alice: dedicated typically takes 4-8 weeks depending on reqs, VPC + SAML SSO and customer-managed KMS add time. we have an on-prem package but most customers use VPC private deployment. we'll share a deployment checklist.
[13:05] Oliver: from finance standpoint, what are the commit options vs pay-as-you-go?
[13:18] Alice: Dedicated is reserved monthly capacity with commit tiers and discounts; hosted is usage-based. we can model expected unit economics and run a what-if for a 12-month commit vs continuing hosted. I'll send numbers.

[16:40] Maya: reliability question — do you have audit logs and per-token provenance for compliance?
[16:50] Priya: yes we provide audit logs, request tracing, and can integrate with your SIEM. SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs will be shared. KMS/HSM support is available for Private deployments.

[19:30] Ravi: another technical detail — our Platform team uses a lot of sagemaker and k8s. how does Redwood integrate with our infra?
[19:42] Tom: we offer SDKs and a consistent API; for private deployments we provide a control plane connector and k8s operators for rollout. there may be some infra work for network egress rules and GPU scheduling.

[23:55] Alice: ok let's look at costs — embedding & rerank workloads are big contributors, plus heavy burst traffic around marketing drops. have you considered caching embedding vectors or using lower-dim embeddings for some jobs?
[24:10] Maya: we tried caching recently but invalidation is tricky with our content churn. any best practices?
[24:20] Tom: yes, use a TTL strategy and shard cache by content hash; we can help with heuristics. also batching small requests into micro-batches reduces per-token cost significantly.

[28:00] Nina: about benchmarks — can Redwood run a P50/P95 benchmark with our payloads? we want reproducible numbers.
[28:12] Tom: absolutely, we recommend a 2-week benchmark window with representative payloads; we'll spin up a dedicated test pool to match your production QPS. we'll need data slices and expected traffic patterns.

[31:30] Ravi: security — SSO and RBAC are critical. can we get per-route RBAC and audit?
[31:40] Priya: yes per-route RBAC is supported in the console; we'll send the RBAC guide. also keep in mind that RBAC + audit logs combo meets most compliance needs.

[34:05] Oliver: if we move to dedicated, what are SLA terms?
[34:14] Alice: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets depending on commit tier; we'll include the SLA appendix in the contract.

[37:00] Maya: roadmap alignment — we're planning a Q4 feature push and want prioritized support for multi-model routing for A/B tests. can Redwood support canary rollouts per-route?
[37:14] Tom: yes, canary and A/B rollout is supported — you can set percentage routing and automatic fallbacks if error rates spike.

[40:20] Ravi: open question — any known limitations with long-context KV cache for our 16k prompt use cases?
[40:33] Tom: long context increases memory and KV cache pressure; our runtime has optimizations but it depends on model and GPU memory. quantization helps but may degrade quality. dedicated instances with larger GPU RAM are recommended for consistent long-context throughput.

[43:50] Nina: billing — we need invoice-level granularity and chargeback tags per team.
[44:00] Alice: we support tags and can produce invoice breakouts per-project. we'll include a sample invoice.

[47:10] Priya: quick recap of decisions: Redwood to run a benchmark, share security docs, and demo dedicated capacity to engineering. Lucent to provide pilot workload and expected SLOs.
[47:25] Maya: yes that's right.

[49:00] Oliver: finance will review the 12-month commit vs hosted run rate once we get your cost model.
[49:12] Alice: I'll include a savings projection in the cost breakdown.

[53:00] Tom: technical note — for the benchmark we'll want to test three modes: hosted baseline, quantized variant, and dedicated pinned model to compare latency and quality.
[53:15] Ravi: agreed. also please include the model versions and exact quantization settings in the results.

[56:30] Alice: ok final next steps and owners in flight: we'll share docs and schedule the demo. thanks everyone.
[56:42] Maya: thanks all.
[56:50] Ravi: thanks, bye.
[56:55] Alice: bye.

End of transcript.
